title: Observation queue + feasibility routing
description: Score observation requests by science priority and feasibility, cut a queue that fits the night, and route time-critical targets to an explicit override decision.
yaml:
apiVersion: ladder.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: wf-astro-01
  title: Observation queue + feasibility routing
  description: Score observation requests by science priority and feasibility, cut a queue that fits the
    night, and route time-critical targets to an explicit override decision.
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  objective: Produce a night plan where every scheduled observation is feasible under the forecast conditions
    and every dropped request names the constraint that excluded it.
  policies:
    maxConcurrency: 4
    onFailure: preserve-completed
    requireApprovalFor:
      - n-approval
  nodes:
    - id: n-intake
      kind: input
      name: Observation requests and conditions
      summary: Observation requests and conditions
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - text
        properties:
          text:
            type: string
            description: The requester's objective, source material, or instructions.
          workflowFields:
            type: object
            required:
              - observation_requests
              - visibility_windows
              - weather_forecast
              - available_hours
            properties:
              observation_requests: {}
              visibility_windows: {}
              weather_forecast: {}
              available_hours: {}
        x-ladder-input-mode: text
    - id: n-classify
      kind: agent
      templateRef: astro-01
      name: Score requests by priority and feasibility
      summary: Score and label every incoming item before anything is queued.
      role: Scheduler allocating telescope time against visibility, conditions, and science priority.
      prompt: You are an Observation Scheduler. You rank observation requests against visibility windows,
        airmass, lunar and weather conditions, instrument configuration, and science priority, and you
        state the specific constraint that excluded any request you dropped. You never schedule an observation
        whose required conditions cannot occur in the window, because an infeasible plan consumes the
        night that a feasible one would have used.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - optimization
          - domain-analysis
          - decision-analysis
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - mcp:observatory-scheduler
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - label
          - severity
          - confidence
          - rationale
        properties:
          label: {}
          severity: {}
          confidence: {}
          rationale: {}
    - id: n-filter
      kind: transform
      name: Drop out-of-scope items
      summary: keep requests whose visibility window and instrument configuration are achievable tonight
      config:
        operation: filter
        expression: keep requests whose visibility window and instrument configuration are achievable
          tonight
    - id: n-rank
      kind: transform
      name: Rank by urgency
      summary: sort by science_priority descending, then by window_closing_time ascending
      config:
        operation: sort
        expression: sort by science_priority descending, then by window_closing_time ascending
    - id: n-queue
      kind: transform
      name: Cut the actionable queue
      summary: take the first available_hours worth of requests as the night queue
      config:
        operation: slice
        expression: take the first available_hours worth of requests as the night queue
    - id: n-severity
      kind: condition
      name: Severity routing
      summary: Route on request.time_criticality selects one declared branch.
      config:
        expression: request.time_criticality selects one declared branch
        branches:
          - label: Escalate
            when: escalate
          - label: Standard
            when: standard
          - label: Default
            when: default
    - id: n-escalate
      kind: agent
      templateRef: astro-04
      name: Time-critical override assessment
      summary: Escalation path for the top band.
      role: Operations analyst managing spacecraft health, contacts, and conjunction risk.
      prompt: You are a Satellite Operations Analyst. You assess spacecraft telemetry against expected
        behavior, plan contact and downlink schedules against real link budgets, and evaluate conjunction
        warnings with the covariance behind them rather than the miss distance alone. You escalate on
        the declared risk threshold instead of waiting for a closer approach, because the maneuver window
        closes before the uncertainty does.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - observability
          - optimization
          - teaching
          - anomaly-detection
          - risk-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - mcp:ground-station
        permissions:
          - explicit-authorization-required
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-handle
      kind: agent
      templateRef: astro-05
      name: Standard queue placement and setup
      summary: Standard resolution path.
      role: Specialist maintaining and validating the calibration chain of an instrument.
      prompt: You are an Instrument Calibration Specialist. You maintain the calibration chain — reference
        standards, transfer, drift, and validity period — and you state the traceability and the epoch
        of every calibration product applied. You invalidate downstream results when a calibration is
        found to be out of date rather than correcting them quietly, because silent recalibration destroys
        the comparability of an archive.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - domain-analysis
          - data-quality-analysis
          - research
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - mcp:archive
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-rejoin
      kind: join
      name: Reconverge after routing
      summary: Release whichever routed path completed.
      config:
        join: first
    - id: n-approval
      kind: approval
      name: Duty astronomer approves the night plan
      summary: Pause for the duty astronomer; on timeout, escalate.
    - id: workflow-output
      kind: output
      name: Released deliverable
      summary: Return the completed Observation queue + feasibility routing deliverable, the evidence
        behind it, and every unresolved item.
  edges:
    - id: wf-astro-01-edge-1
      from: n-intake
      to: n-classify
      kind: data
    - id: wf-astro-01-edge-2
      from: n-classify
      to: n-filter
      kind: data
    - id: wf-astro-01-edge-3
      from: n-filter
      to: n-rank
      kind: data
    - id: wf-astro-01-edge-4
      from: n-rank
      to: n-queue
      kind: data
    - id: wf-astro-01-edge-5
      from: n-queue
      to: n-severity
      kind: data
    - id: wf-astro-01-edge-6
      from: n-severity
      to: n-escalate
      kind: control
      condition: escalate
    - id: wf-astro-01-edge-7
      from: n-severity
      to: n-handle
      kind: control
      condition: standard
    - id: wf-astro-01-edge-8
      from: n-escalate
      to: n-rejoin
      kind: data
    - id: wf-astro-01-edge-9
      from: n-handle
      to: n-rejoin
      kind: data
    - id: wf-astro-01-edge-10
      from: n-rejoin
      to: n-approval
      kind: data
    - id: wf-astro-01-edge-11
      from: n-approval
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
      condition: approved
